item.title: Best Core Keeper Starting Seed — Seeds for a Smooth First Session (1.3.0.6)
item.description: A good starting seed buys you the first hour of Core Keeper: loot close to the Core, a peaceful meadow to grab early wool and milk, and no 20-tunnel dig just to find copper. This page lists the community-verified starting seeds we trust — every entry traces back to a Reddit, Discord or press roundup source. For how seeds actually shape your world, read the Seeds guide. Why we recommend these seeds Seed What you get Who it’s for 400957925946 Useful starter items near spawn First-timers who want a frictionless opening 1 Meadow sub-biome north of the Core Anyone who wants Moolin / Bambuck immediately 186511372992 Meadow sub-biome southeast of the Core Fallback if seed 1 feels cramped None of these “cheat” the game — they just put the fixed, seed-locked features (a meadow, starter chests) on a short leash from The Core.

item.title: Core Keeper Automation Guide — Auto Farms, Drills and Power Circuits That Actually Work
item.description: Once your base has smelters and chests, the next time sink is feeding them. This automation guide goes past the basics: how power actually travels, which machines to put on the Automation Table, and four farm layouts — ore boulders, wood, crops and mobs — that run while you explore. How electricity really works Every automation machine needs a powered tile next to it (or a run of Electrical Wire). Powered machines show yellow notches on the four sides of their base.

item.title: Core Keeper Base Building Guide — Room Rules, NPC Housing and Automation
item.description: A good Core Keeper base is more than a pile of chests. This base building guide covers the room system, NPC move-in rules, bed mechanics and the automation basics that keep your underground hub running while you explore. Room rules that actually matter Rooms are the core building block of a Core Keeper base. The game recognizes a room when: The enclosed area is between 2×2 and 8×8 tiles (smaller or larger rooms don’t register) It has a door and a bed It contains the required item for the NPC you want (each NPC has a specific item) No players are within 30 tiles of the room for roughly a minute If any condition fails, the room won’t count — and NPCs won’t move in.

item.title: Core Keeper Boss Fight Strategy — How to Beat Every Boss, Positioning and Gear
item.description: The boss guide covers where each boss lives, how to summon it and what it drops. This strategy guide is the fight itself: the health pools, the attack numbers, the enrage thresholds, and the positioning that turns a wipe into a farm. Rules that apply to almost every boss Enrage at a threshold. Most bosses switch to a faster, deadlier phase once you push them below a health percentage — the fight gets harder near the end, not easier.

item.title: Core Keeper Boss Guide — All 7 Bosses, Drops, Locations and Strategies
item.description: Core Keeper’s boss order follows your tool progression: three bosses around the Core must fall before it powers up, then the outer-ring titans open endgame content. This Core Keeper boss guide lists every boss, where they spawn, how to summon them and what they drop. The three early bosses (power up the Core) Defeat all three and place their drops on the effigies next to the Core to activate it.

item.title: Core Keeper Co-op Guide — Multiplayer Scaling, Division of Labour and Shared Progress
item.description: Core Keeper is built for the couch-cave loop: three friends, one Core, nobody agreeing on where the farm goes. This co-op guide covers what multiplayer actually changes mechanically (spawns, boss health, save ownership), what stays personal, and how to split roles so your party moves faster than two solo players would. What co-op changes — and what it doesn’t Verified multiplayer rules from the combat mechanics: Mechanic Single player In co-op Regular mob health / damage Base values Unchanged — no inflation Local ambient spawn rate 1× around you ~2× with two players standing together — everyone triggers their own spawns Boss health Base Scales up by player count, with a different multiplier per boss Hard mode tag Fixed at world creation Same for everyone; the tag lives in the world save Seasonal / calendar settings Your calendar Host’s (or server’s) setting takes priority for everyone NPCs, rooms, seasonal merchant In your world In the host’s world — everyone trades there The practical surprise is spawn rate, not boss numbers: splitting up across the map is safer than travelling together, because clustered players feel like a spotlight drawing mobs from every tunnel.

item.title: Core Keeper Cooking & Food Buff Guide — Best Recipes and How Buffs Stack
item.description: Food in Core Keeper isn’t just hunger — the right dishes are pre-boss loadouts. This cooking guide explains how food buffs work, which ingredients give the strongest effects, and the best combos before each fight. How food buffs work Food value refills your hunger; hunger loss only reduces max health and stats — you can’t die of starvation. Cooked ingredients give Regen, max health, armor, damage and speed buffs with a duration.

item.title: Core Keeper First Hour Guide — World Creation, Tools and Your First Boss
item.description: The Core Keeper getting started experience is built around one loop: craft a workbench, make stronger tools, mine tougher walls, find better ores, and repeat. This guide walks through world creation, the first hour, and the three early bosses you need to beat before the Core powers up. World creation: what to pick Select Start Game from the main menu to create a world. You can also join a friend’s world from the Steam friends list — Core Keeper has native multiplayer with no dedicated server required, and more than the officially stated 8 players can connect.

item.title: Core Keeper Fishing Guide — Best Spots, Bait, the Fishing Workbench and Rare Fish
item.description: Fishing in Core Keeper is more than a side activity: it is a second ore income, a key source of accessories, and the only way to summon Omoroth later. This advanced Core Keeper fishing guide explains how the catch system decides what you pull out, how to set up a fishing corner, and which water to stand in for the rare fish and valuables you actually want. item.title: Core Keeper Gear Progression Guide — Copper to Solarite Armor and Weapon Tiers
item.description: Gear in Core Keeper follows the same ring-biome ore ladder as mining: copper → tin/bronze → iron → scarlet → octarine → galaxite → solarite. This gear progression guide maps each tier to its armor set, the weapon worth crafting, and the accessory slots that actually move your build — so you stop wasting bars on upgrades you’ll wear for ten minutes. Armor sets by tier Every armor piece breaks down the same way: a helm, a chest and pants, each with its own durability.

item.title: Core Keeper Greenhouse Guide — Crop Layout, Harvest Chance and Golden Crop Profit
item.description: A greenhouse is where Core Keeper shifts from “scavenge food” to “manufacture buffs.” This advanced guide covers the growth cycle, picking crops by ground type, stacking harvest chance for throughput, and laying out plots so watering never becomes a chore. The 10-minute growth cycle Once you water a seed, the timer runs on its own — you can leave and come back: Stage Time Watered seed → sprout 2 minutes Sprout → pre-harvest 4 minutes Pre-harvest → harvestable 4 minutes Every manual harvest grants gardening experience.

item.title: Core Keeper Mining Guide — Wall Hardness, Drill Efficiency and the Best Digging Routes
item.description: The ore tier guide tells you which ore lives in which ring. This guide goes deeper: how mining damage actually resolves against walls, how to plan tunnels so you never waste swings, and how drills turn ore boulders into an infinite late-game ore supply. How wall damage really works A wall does not have a simple health bar. Every hit first deducts a flat resistance, and only the leftover damage bites into wall health.

item.title: Core Keeper Mods Guide — Where to Download, How to Install and Essential Mods
item.description: Core Keeper supports official modding through Steam Workshop and mod.io, with community content managed by the CoreLib framework. This modding guide covers where to find mods, how to install them, and the most useful quality-of-life mods. Where to get mods Platform What it is Notes Steam Workshop Official in-game mod browser One-click subscribe & install; requires the game mod.io Cross-platform mod repository Browsable online, official Core Keeper page CoreLib Community mod framework / loader Most mods depend on it; install first Check the Mods hub for an indexed list of popular mods and their patch compatibility.

item.description: Core Keeper’s towns don’t grow by themselves: every settled resident moves in because you built the right room, put the right item in it, and walked away long enough for them to notice. item.title: Core Keeper Ore Tier Guide — Pickaxe Progression and Where Each Ore Spawns
item.description: Core Keeper’s world is generated in rings around the Core, and each ring holds different ores. This Core Keeper ore guide maps every ore to the pickaxe tier and biome you need — so you never waste time mining with the wrong tool. Pickaxe tiers at a glance Pickaxe Workbench Materials Mines Wood Pickaxe Starting inventory Wood Soft dirt walls only Copper Pickaxe Basic Workbench 8 Copper Bar, 10 Wood Copper, Tin Tin Pickaxe Basic Workbench 8 Tin Bar, 10 Wood Iron Iron Pickaxe Iron Anvil 8 Iron Bar, 10 Wood Gold, Scarlet Gold Pickaxe Gold Anvil 8 Gold Bar, 10 Wood Harder ores, faster Scarlet Pickaxe Scarlet Workbench 8 Scarlet Bar, 10 Wood Best pre-endgame speed You can technically mine anywhere from the start — but stronger walls block exploration until your pickaxe tier catches up.

item.title: Core Keeper World Seeds Guide — How Seeds Shape Your World
item.description: Every Core Keeper world is generated from a seed — the number you pick at world creation. The seed decides where each biome ring sits, which direction you find the Clay Caves, and roughly where the early bosses spawn. This guide explains how seed generation works and how to use seeds with friends. What a seed controls Aspect Seed-dependent Biome angles Yes — Clay Caves / Forgotten Ruins each occupy half of the world beyond the chasm; the exact angle varies by seed Outer biome order Yes — the three outer biomes (Azeos’ Wilderness, Sunken Sea, Mold) rotate counter-clockwise per seed Boss placement Partly — Glurch spawns ~65 tiles in a random angle; boss arc segments shift with the seed World shape / ring distances No — the ring band structure (0–140, 150–450, 450–520, 520–1200+) is the same for every world In short: the seed is a rotation and placement key, not a terrain generator.
